sources.parts: By the model (bin/lib/hulls/currach.py): 8.6 m² of hide 5 mm thick at 860 kg/m³, 37 kg, over 21 ribs, 7 stringers and two gunwales of laths 1 by 6 cm, 81 m of ash, and a thwart pole 9 cm across, 38 kg: 75 kg
sources.swimmingOffsetY: Drawn at the draft she floats at with one aboard, 0.043 m (bin/lib/hulls/currach.py): vanilla floats a boat with the water 0.018 m over her selection box's top less this offset
sources.shell: Raw cowhide is 2 to 6 mm thick. A blow springs back off the hide unless a lath backs it where it lands: by the model, ribs 0.8 voxel wide every 3 and three stringers a side back 40% of her sides, the ribs and the keelson 31% of her bottom. A breaker presses the hide onto the laths, each 1 cm deep bending over the 0.15 m between stringers
sources.depthMetres: Keel to gunwale amidships, by the model (bin/lib/hulls/currach.py)
sources.waterplaneSquareMetres: So that her 1878 L hold full, with one aboard, brings her gunwale to the water (bin/lib/hulls/physics.py)
sources.seep: A seam where one hide meets the next weeps once the tallow has washed out of it, and Aran crews dressed their currachs every few days: a seam across her, some 2.3 m of it, 15 L an hour. A currach from before her build is covered in prepared hide over her eight sections, with the two seams the three large hides of her old recipe had
sources.cover: The hides a vessel is covered with as her build lays them; one from before her build is covered with prepared hides, as the grid made her

sources.heave: A hide hull of 75 kg sits on the water and rises with the crest: it rides over seas that board heavier boats
sources.capsizeBreakerMetres: Aran currachs are launched and landed through breaking surf: the light, flared hull lifts to a breaker that rolls a heavier boat of its beam
sources.rollResponse: A beamy, light hull rolls with the sea about as much as vanilla's boats
sources.pitchResponse: The light, flexing hull follows the swell bow and stern

sources.capacityLitres: Her hollow inside the hide up to her gunwale amidships, where water first spills over, by the model (bin/lib/hulls/currach.py)
sources.deckSquareMetres: Her opening at the gunwale catches the rain, by the model (bin/lib/hulls/currach.py)
sources.drainLitresPerHour: Greased hide is watertight; the wear of an ungreased hull is upkeep, not a leak

sources.time: A held action lasts the real time of that one piece of work over sixty: game time runs 30 times faster than real time, and boat work is halved again
sources.layout: A currach's gunwale was laid out on the ground first and her ribs set into it (Hornell 1938, the Boyne currach woven round its gunwale on the ground): two long laths laid side by side as far apart as her model draws her gunwale laths, 1.14 m, to within a step of the 1/16 m the bed lays laths by, whose ends at the bow the first rope draws together; astern they run straight on until the second rope draws them together there
sources.endLashing: Each end bound with some ten metres of cord, a quarter of an hour's work (an estimate)
sources.ribs: Fitting one rib, about three minutes, as the canoe's: currach ribs were scalded, bent over the gunwale and set into it, built upside down (the Boyne and Aran currachs). Bent in wet, they hold their bend once dry, in a couple of days
sources.cover: Stretching and sewing a small hide's worth of cover, some twenty minutes (an estimate); a bigger hide covers more at once and takes as much longer
sources.lacing: The hide laced to the gunwale at short intervals (Hornell 1938), every 5 cm, each turn round the gunwale and the hide's edge: the shape's builder counts the rope
sources.overturned: Built upside down, her gunwale on the ground, she is turned over before she goes afloat (the Boyne currach was lifted out and turned upright to be covered; Aran currachs are carried upside down)
sources.framePart: Her frame is the wood of her laths: its share and the weight it was set for are ash's, its strength and density are those of the wood split
